summary: Comprehensive e2e testing for AIA Legnano platform. Backend: 29/29 pytest tests passed (100%) covering admin auth, public endpoints (settings/nav/articles/events/officials/members/designations/stats), forms (corso-arbitri lead + contatti), admin CRUD for articles/events/officials/members/designations, HTML sanitization of bodyHtml, lead status update, settings PUT round-trip. Frontend Playwright: 16/16 public scenarios passed (home hero, CTA, news list/detail with proper paragraph spacing, diventa-arbitro form submit + lead-success page, chi-siamo, designazioni filtering, associati listing and profile, eventi, contatti, admin login bad/good creds + redirect, dashboard with 9/9 sidebar items, logout). Admin flows: 7/9 passed (login, articles list, new article open, tiptap editor visible+typing, preview, leads visible with Mario, messages page, settings phone update reflects in public footer). CRITICAL BUG FOUND: creating a new article via /admin/articles/new sends PUT /api/admin/articles/undefined instead of POST /api/admin/articles — route mismatch in App.js.

ui_bugs.issue: Creating a new article via /admin/articles/new fails silently: the form save handler calls PUT /api/admin/articles/undefined (returns 200 but no document updated, no redirect, no error shown) instead of POST /api/admin/articles. Root cause: App.js declares two routes: `articles/new` (no :id param) and `articles/:id`. When route `articles/new` matches, useParams() returns {id: undefined}; therefore `isNew = id === 'new'` evaluates to false → handler goes through the update branch. Confirmed via backend access log entries `PUT /api/admin/articles/undefined HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.

issues: After updating site settings phone, footer briefly shows two phone numbers in inner_text (probably from a stacked Telefono + map/CTA element). Functional impact: none — footer DOES contain the new phone — but worth a visual review of SiteFooter rendering.

action_items: FIX (App.js, lines 55-57): remove the dedicated `articles/new` route OR change `isNew` logic in AdminArticleEditPage to `const isNew = !id || id === 'new';`. Recommended fix: keep only `articles/:id` route — react-router-dom matches `/admin/articles/new` to it with `id='new'`. Remove line 56 (`<Route path="articles/new" element={<AdminArticleEditPage />} />`).
OPTIONAL: add data-testid attributes to AdminSettingsPage inputs (phone, email, etc.) for easier automated testing.
OPTIONAL: investigate footer rendering when reading inner_text — possible duplicate phone display.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js routing bug: `articles/new` declared as a separate route without :id param causes useParams() to return id=undefined, breaking the isNew flag in AdminArticleEditPage and silently failing new-article creation through the UI.

AdminArticleEditPage.save(): backend returns 200 OK even when PUT id doesn't match any document — frontend never knows the save did nothing. Consider returning 404 on no-match in admin update endpoints, or checking result.matched_count.

Backend public.get_settings() uses a non-standard first lookup `find_one({"_id": 0}, ...)` (line 18) which is logically a no-op filter — works only because of fallback at line 20. Could be simplified.
Form fields in AdminSettingsPage lack data-testid attributes — reduces test reliability.

One left-over draft article 'TEST articolo 2ebb4230' may remain in the database because UI save flow created it via the PUT-undefined path (article was never actually inserted, but slugified test articles from manual POST were cleaned).

For frontend, the only failing flow is creating a NEW article via /admin/articles/new — verify after main agent fixes the routing/isNew bug. After fix, re-run the lead+article+settings admin flow.
rca_of_the_issue: BUG: New article creation broken. RCA: react-router-dom v6 matches routes most-specific first. The route `articles/new` (no :id param) matches the URL `/admin/articles/new` BEFORE `articles/:id` would. Component AdminArticleEditPage uses `const { id } = useParams()` — but that route declaration has no `:id` segment → id is `undefined`. The variable `isNew = id === 'new'` is then `false`, so on Salva click the handler calls `adminUpdateArticle(undefined, payload)` which hits `PUT /api/admin/articles/undefined`. Mongo update_one with `{id: 'undefined'}` matches 0 docs, returns 200, frontend stays on /admin/articles/new with no feedback. REPRO: 1) login /admin/login as admin 2) go to /admin/articles 3) click 'Nuovo articolo' 4) fill title and content 5) click Salva. Observed: URL stays at /admin/articles/new, no redirect, no error. Expected: redirect to /admin/articles/{new_id} with the article persisted. MITIGATION: remove `<Route path="articles/new" .../>` OR fix isNew check as described above.
